newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees record Colombia 97/8 cotton import.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees record Colombia 97/8 cotton import.

text.p: An agricultural attache at the American embassy in Bogota forecast Colombia cotton imports would climb to a record 50,000 tonnes in marketing season 1997/98 (August-July) from 42,000 tonnes in 1996/97.

In a report dated June 10 released in Washington on Thursday, the attache noted about 55 percent of all imports during 1996/97 will be supplied by the United States, up from 48 percent a year earlier.
Over the next three to five years, Colombia cotton imports are projected to grow at an annual rate of five to 10 percent.

Colombia cotton output has trended downward since the 1970's, the attache said. Cotton production fell to 55,000 tonnes in 1996/97, 22 percent below the prior year. The outlook for 1997/98 is for a further reduction to 40,000 tonnes, the attache said, citing an expected decline in planted area.
"The industry is trying to stabilize its production at current levels, but we anticipate that output is likely to decline at an annual rate of 1-2 percent over the next 3-5 years," the attache wrote.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
